findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
findings.body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil, and the next line immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. A TopicUser row is only created once a user has visited/interacted with a topic, yet the unsubscribe link is included in every notification email — e.g. a user who was mentioned or invited to a topic but never opened it will have no row. Clicking the emailed 'stop receiving notifications' link then raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of unsubscribing them. The code should fall back to TopicUser.change(...)/create the row with the desired level.

findings.title: Notification state is mutated by an unauthenticated-CSRF-able GET request, and refresh re-toggles it
findings.body: The `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route is a GET that flips the user's notification_level (watching/tracking -> regular, regular/muted -> muted) with no CSRF token or confirmation. Because it is a plain GET with session cookies, any logged-in user can have their topic notification settings silently changed just by loading a URL — e.g. an attacker can embed `` in a post or external page and the victim's browser will hit the endpoint and mute/unwatch the topic. Additionally, since the same GET both performs the toggle and renders the unsubscribe page, every page refresh or link re-visit toggles the level again (watching -> regular -> muted), so the user's final state depends on how many times the URL was loaded. State changes should not happen on GET (or should be idempotent, e.g. always mute).

findings.title: Email copy promises to stop notifications but the endpoint only downgrades to regular
findings.body: The new unsubscribe_link text says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here', but TopicsController#unsubscribe only sets watching/tracking users to `regular` — a level that still emails the user when someone replies to them or @mentions them. A user who clicks the link believing they will no longer receive emails for that topic will keep getting reply/mention notifications, which is a trust/warranty problem for the feature. Either the endpoint should set the level to muted, or the message should accurately describe what will still be received.

findings.title: Unsubscribe link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} and raises for callers that don't supply it
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` locale now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. I18n raises `MissingInterpolationArgument` when an interpolation key in the translation has no value, so any caller that builds an email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without passing `unsubscribe_url` will now fail to render and the email send will blow up. The only in-repo caller was updated (and the message_builder spec had to be amended to pass `unsubscribe_url`), but MessageBuilder is a reusable API used by plugins and mailers that set `add_unsubscribe_link` on its own; the builder should default `unsubscribe_url` (e.g. to the user preferences URL) or use `I18n.t(..., unsubscribe_url: ... )` with a fallback so missing values degrade gracefully.

findings.title: No request specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The TopicsController#unsubscribe action introduces new routing, access control (ensure_logged_in), a toggle rule based on the current notification level, and a 301 redirect for slug mismatch, but no controller/request specs were added for it — the only test change in the PR is unrelated (adding unsubscribe_url to a message_builder spec). Notably, the nil-TopicUser case and the watching->regular vs regular->muted toggle behavior are completely untested, which is how the nil crash above ships unnoticed.
